chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man goes out for trade to Makkah, or he has camels which he hires out; is his Hajj deficient or complete?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but his Hajj is complete.'

key_terms.يُكْرِيهَا: He hires them out / rents them

ai.seo_question: Is a man's Hajj considered complete if he is engaged in trade or hiring out his camels during the pilgrimage?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that engaging in trade or managing livestock does not detract from the validity of one's Hajj, addressing concerns that worldly pursuits might render the pilgrimage deficient. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Hajj remains complete provided the essential pillars are fulfilled, even if the pilgrim is occupied with lawful economic activities. It highlights the practical flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the integration of daily livelihood with religious obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man goes out to Makkah regarding business, or there happens to be a camel for him which he has hired. Would his Hajj be deficient or complete?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but his Hajj is complete’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who goes out for trade to Makkah or that he has a camel that he has given for hire to transport people; if his al-Hajj is complete or defective. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, but it is complete al-Hajj.’”
